title: How would you estimate how many laptops UK university students buy each year?
description: A step-by-step estimate for "How many laptops do UK university students buy each year?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: A replacement-cycle question with a natural anchor: most students buy one laptop per degree. Have a go at your own estimate before reading on.
body:
The question

How many laptops do UK university students buy each year?

The approach

Students ÷ years between laptop purchases.

Tip: Keep your page tidy: one line per step, the running total circled at the end.

Step by step

  1. University students in the UK: 2.9M
  2. ÷ 3 years between laptop purchases

That gives about 967k laptops a year.

Does it make sense?

Roughly one laptop per student per degree, which is what most students would say.

Avoid assuming every student buys a new machine

Dividing 2.9 million students by three years gives roughly 967,000 laptops annually, but it quietly assumes all students own a laptop, buy a new one every three years and purchase only while enrolled. In reality, some bring a laptop bought before university and others use a shared or refurbished device.

An alternative build starts with new entrants. Imagine 900,000 people begin courses each year; 60% buy a laptop specifically for university, giving 540,000 entrant purchases. Suppose another 200,000 continuing students replace machines unexpectedly. That produces 740,000 annual student-related purchases. These are invented assumptions to illustrate a different method, not an estimate of current enrolments.

Ask whether the case concerns purchases made by students in a year, laptops bought specifically because of university, or the installed base of student laptops. Those definitions can produce different answers even when the arithmetic is sound.
